purpose: Independent engineering memory-admission gate; no latency ranking or paper performance measurement.

verifier.positive_fixture: Completed C1024 resident subset: 32 requests, 16 phases, 1388 source files.
negative_fixtures: zero-memory phase with hidden CUDA allocation

copy_verifier.method: All data/log/profile targets absent before copy; exact file-set equality and SHA256 equality of every source/destination file; original manifests unmodified.

workload.model_scope: 10 independently copied real checkpoint dense blocks using source-layer hidden/residual input replay; embedding, final norm, all candidate hidden and last-token LM head. Not a trained ten-layer model or full 61-layer validation.
workload.access_trace: users 0 through 15 twice, sequential; revisit identity independent of cache miss
workload.dtype: BF16 main KV, 576 elements per token, 1152 bytes per token
workload.warmup: One full request per case, then a new empty cache
workload.profiled_phases: prefill on actual miss, then extend/truncate/session_metrics

numerical_boundary.note: C512 is supplemental resident memory coverage; its reference/self comparison does not validate an offload path or eligibility for cross-C performance ranking.

cpu_and_pinned_accounting.pinned_allocator_capacity_rule: Independent next power of two of owned storage bytes at installed torch 2.12.1+cu130 / 7269437d655783a26cba32aa88195b741ff496aa
cpu_and_pinned_accounting.dynamic_pinned_rule: Reconcile cumulative handouts to validated Python scalar and native nonzero/unique synchronous call lifetimes; report simultaneous peaks rather than cumulative handouts.

coverage_and_bounds.direct: C1024/W1024 all four schemes; C2048/W2048 all four schemes under fixed-workspace protocol; C512/W512 resident only; C256/W256 resident and dense-prefetch.
coverage_and_bounds.same_geometry_equivalence: The sampled C2048/W2048 fixed protocol has the same query geometry and reservation as per-chunk C2048/W2048; no second GPU run is claimed.
largest_fixed_inventory_anchors: C256 and C512 resident reach the maximum four retained users.
C1024 ECHO and serial_sparse reach all sixteen retained users with the same fixed NH/P and per-session capacity used at smaller C.
C256 dense_prefetch reaches the maximum fifteen retained users.

shape_bound.additional_sparse_metadata_workspace: Fixed by NH and P; independent of C at the configured arena/pool geometry.
shape_bound.session_and_pinned_capacity: Fixed by 65664-token capacity, scheme and retained-user count; independent of C.

unsampled_per_chunk.support: Same sixteen-user fixed inventory as directly sampled C1024, smaller declared Q workspace, and exact CPU planning rows under both hard budgets. These are analytic reservation bounds, not direct allocator observations at those C values.

Fourteen-user fixed inventory is below sampled C256 fifteen-user inventory; Q512 workspace lies between directly sampled Q256 and Q1024. Its own ledger totals are checked against the hard budgets. Endpoint peaks are not interpolated or added as a claimed measured peak.

unsampled_fixed_2048.support: All source planner rows have the identical W2048 reservation and fixed capacity counts as sampled C2048/W2048: 2/15/15/7 users. Q<=2048 is within the declared monotone execution bound. No complete trace or allocator peak was directly sampled for these fixed-W smaller-C cases.

coverage_and_bounds.bound_limit: Coverage arguments apply only to the declared allocator/shape contract and fixed 64K+128 workload, NH/P, layer count, dtype, checkpoint and runtime identity. They do not prove unseen allocation branches, numerical equivalence across C, latency, arbitrary histories, or total process memory.

limits: Profiler covers four request IDs per case, while all 32 requests execute and retain admission checks; it does not observe every request allocation.
Direct library allocations outside PyTorch allocators, pageable malloc overhead, Python objects and allocator internal bookkeeping remain outside the observer.
Weights and ordinary activations are outside the cache hard budget; process CUDA allocated/reserved peaks are separate fields.
Owned pinned capacity differs from globally retained pinned allocator blocks; active current/peak counters are unreliable in this installed allocator.
Saved nonresident output tensors are not available for offline numerical recomputation; exact comparisons executed inline against independent same-C resident outputs.
Independent verifier checks saved source bytes, structural raw evidence, complete phase coverage and arithmetic; it does not rerun the model or reconstruct allocation lifetimes from scratch.

Freeze04 changed diagnostic tooling; freeze05 adds complete ordinal allocation matching. Runtime identity is unchanged; the three original gates retain freeze03 identities and the new C256 gate retains freeze05 identity. No manifest is re-signed.

observer_revision_evidence.matching_rule: Complete per-address CUDA allocation ordinal bijection, including ordinary allocations, with equal generation counts, requested bytes fitting profiler rounded blocks, identical requested-free state, and valid allocation/completed-free order. No widened cross-clock tolerance. Active lifetime uses only history time; pending frees remain live.

discarded_diagnostic.cause: Profiler allocation time lagged history allocation time by about 12 microseconds and could be 1-3 microseconds later than requested free; complete allocation sequences were present.

acceptance_sidecar_boundary.note: Added after complete byte-identical copy verification. Original manifest and files are unmodified; new sidecar files have their own manifest and hashes. Copy file-set counts refer to original frozen artifacts only.
